tests.notes: Thick film (Giemsa) or Knott's/membrane-filtration concentration. Lymphatic filariasis is a Ugandan elimination target; Mansonella perstans is common and usually incidental. minLevel judgement.

orderLoinc.longName: Trypanosoma sp identified in Cerebrospinal Fluid by Wet preparation

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: Staging also uses CSF WBC count (S1 body fluid counts) - order together. Examine within 20 min (trypanosomes lyse). minLevel judgement.

tests.container: FIT sampling device or clean stool container

orderLoinc.longName: Hemoglobin [Presence] in Stool from gastrointestinal lower by Immunoassay

tests.notes: Immunochemical cassette; no dietary restriction. Available in private labs and larger hospitals. minLevel judgement.

tests.specimen: Fresh stool (ideally 2 slides from each of 2-3 days)

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: Quantifies S. mansoni and soil-transmitted helminth intensity (WHO classes); mostly used by the MoH Vector Control Division and in endemic-district hospitals around Lakes Victoria/Albert and the Nile. obs.stool_op_wet_prep reused to record species seen. No order LOINC.

orderLoinc.longName: Microscopic observation [Identifier] in Blood by Malaria smear

tests.notes: Giemsa thick film for detection and density (parasites per 200/500 WBC), thin film for species. Reuses v1 species and density concepts unchanged.

orderLoinc.longName: Plasmodium sp Ag [Identifier] in Blood by Rapid immunoassay

tests.notes: HRP2 (Pf) / pLDH (Pan) cassette; also run by VHTs/iCCM. HRP2 stays positive for weeks after treatment - not for test-of-cure.

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: Recommended section is PARASITOLOGY, not immunology_serology: it is an antigen test for a parasite, used alongside Kato-Katz stool microscopy, the same way the malaria RDT sits in parasitology. Detects S. mansoni (intestinal); not reliable for S. haematobium. Mostly used in mapping/surveys (MoH Vector Control Division) around Lake Victoria, Lake Albert and the Nile; few hospital labs stock it, hence 'referred' with no fixed referral lab. No LOINC term (local code).

tests.specimen: Semen by masturbation after 2-7 days abstinence, delivered within 1 h at body temperature

orderLoinc.longName: Semen analysis fertility panel

tests.notes: WHO 2021 (6th ed.) basic examination: motility reported as progressive / non-progressive / immotile (no a/b grades). restricted=srh proposed. minLevel judgement.

tests.specimen: Bloodless skin snips (iliac crests/calves), incubated in saline
tests.container: Microtitre plate well or small tube with saline

orderLoinc.longName: Filaria identified in Skin by Light microscopy

tests.notes: Mainly MoH onchocerciasis elimination programme (Vector Control Division) surveillance; transmission interrupted in most Ugandan foci, so rarely a routine hospital test. Ov16 serology is immunology_serology.

tests.display: Stool formol-ether concentration for ova and parasites

orderLoinc.longName: Ova and parasites identified in Stool by Concentration

tests.notes: Separate orderable because many HC III labs do only direct wet preps. Use when wet prep is negative but helminths are suspected. minLevel judgement.

tests.display: Stool microscopy for ova and parasites (wet prep)
tests.specimen: Fresh stool (examine within 30 min if watery/bloody, for trophozoites)

orderLoinc.longName: Ova and parasites identified in Stool by Light microscopy

tests.notes: Saline and Lugol's iodine direct wet preps with macroscopy.

orderLoinc.longName: Coccidia identified in Stool by Acid fast stain

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: Key for chronic diarrhoea in advanced HIV and malnourished children. minLevel judgement.

orderLoinc.longName: Urinalysis macro (dipstick) panel - Urine

tests.notes: Section: parasitology. In Ugandan hospital labs the urine strip is read on the microscopy/parasitology bench with urine and stool microscopy (one 'urine R/E' workflow), not on the chemistry analyser bench; quantitative urine chemistry (UACR, urine protein) stays clinical_chemistry. HC II level reflects ANC proteinuria/glucose screening.

tests.display: Urinalysis (urine R/E: macroscopy, dipstick and microscopy)

orderLoinc.longName: Urinalysis complete panel - Urine

tests.notes: Mirrors how Ugandan clinicians order 'urine R/E' as one request. Built from test.urinalysis_dipstick + test.urine_microscopy concepts plus colour/appearance.

orderLoinc.longName: Schistosoma sp identified in Urine sediment by Light microscopy

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: Sedimentation or filtration (10 mL). In Uganda S. mansoni dominates; S. haematobium is limited to small foci, so low volume - judgement.

orderLoinc.longName: Urinalysis microscopic panel - Urine sediment

tests.notes: orderLoinc 24365-9 is DISCOURAGED in LOINC (child panel of the complete urinalysis panels) - kept unverified; most orders should use test.urinalysis_complete. Centrifuged sediment, read at x10/x40.

tests.container: Sterile plain tube or cryovial; 2–8 °C (freeze if delayed); separate aliquot from culture/CrAg

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: Mainly used for meningitis surveillance and when antibiotics were given before LP (culture negative). Does not replace Gram stain, culture, CrAg or Xpert Ultra on CSF. Referral lab and route are judgements; it may also run at the Mulago surveillance sentinel lab or a private syndromic panel lab.

tests.specimen: First-void urine; endocervical or vaginal swab (clinician- or self-collected); urethral swab
tests.container: Kit-specific transport tube (e.g. Xpert CT/NG urine or swab transport reagent)

orderLoinc.longName: Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae DNA panel - Specimen

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: The public sector mainly manages STIs syndromically. NAAT is used at private labs, research sites and some GeneXpert sites. Positive NG with treatment failure → culture and sensitivity (microbiology). minLevel and route are judgements.

tests.specimen: Whole blood (EDTA); oral swab from a deceased suspect
tests.container: EDTA (purple) PLASTIC tube only; triple packaging (Category A, UN2814)
tests.notes: HIGH-RISK SPECIMEN ROUTE, as for the VHF panel. Outbreak-focused order. The 2026 outbreak strain is Bundibugyo virus, so Bundibugyo is listed first; the Zaire-only GeneXpert Ebola cartridge will NOT detect it. Used for case confirmation and for the repeat tests required before discharge under the national EVD protocol.

tests.specimen: Sputum (also CSF, gastric aspirate or stool in children, lymph node aspirate, pleural fluid, urine per national algorithm)
tests.container: Sterile wide-mouth sputum container (falcon tube for CSF/gastric aspirate)

orderLoinc.longName: MTB complex DNA and rpoB RIF resistance mutation panel [Presence]

tests.notes: First test for presumptive TB. Facilities without a machine send the sample via the hub to the nearest GeneXpert site. 'Trace' results are read in clinical context (repeat in adults living with HIV / children per the algorithm). If RIF resistance is detected, send a sample for Xpert MTB/XDR or LPA plus culture/DST at NTRL. minLevel is a judgement based on the GeneXpert network.

tests.container: EDTA (purple) or plain (red); separate and freeze if delayed

orderLoinc.longName: Hepatitis B virus DNA [Units/volume] (viral load) in Serum or Plasma by NAA with probe detection

tests.notes: For HBsAg-positive patients: treatment eligibility (with ALT, APRI/fibrosis), pregnancy (tenofovir prophylaxis threshold) and monitoring. Report in IU/mL. Also offered by private labs. Route is a judgement.

orderLoinc.longName: Hepatitis C virus RNA [Units/volume] (viral load) in Serum or Plasma by NAA with probe detection

tests.notes: Confirms active infection after a reactive anti-HCV (obs.hcv_ab), and is repeated 12 weeks after DAA treatment (SVR12). Some sites run point-of-care GeneXpert HCV VL. Route is a judgement.

tests.specimen: Plasma (EDTA); DBS where the lab validates it
tests.container: EDTA (purple) ×2 (≥4 mL blood), plasma frozen; cold chain via hub

orderLoinc.longName: HIV 1 RNA reverse transcriptase and protease and integrase gene mutations detected [Identifier] in Plasma by Sequencing

tests.notes: Referral only, ordered after confirmed virological failure (VL ≥1000 copies/mL after enhanced adherence counselling) per the national switch process, usually with switch-committee approval. Amplification fails at low VL. Report is a mutation list plus a drug-by-drug interpretation.

tests.specimen: Dried blood spot (heel/toe/finger prick) or EDTA capillary/whole blood for POC
tests.container: DBS filter card (5 fully filled circles, air-dried, glassine + zip bag with desiccant); EDTA microtainer for POC

orderLoinc.longName: HIV 1 RNA+proviral DNA [Presence] in Blood by NAA with probe detection

tests.notes: For HIV-exposed infants under 18 months; antibody tests are not valid at this age. DBS goes via the hub to CPHL. Some facilities have point-of-care EID (GeneXpert HIV-1 Qual, m-PIMA). A positive result means start ART immediately and send a confirmatory sample. Request form needs the infant's age, feeding status and PMTCT prophylaxis. minLevel/route is a judgement.

tests.specimen: Plasma (EDTA); dried blood spot (DBS) where plasma logistics fail
tests.container: EDTA (purple) ×1–2, plasma separated within 6 h (or PPT white top); DBS card for remote sites

orderLoinc.longName: HIV 1 RNA [#/volume] (viral load) in Serum or Plasma by NAA with probe detection

tests.notes: Goes to CPHL via the national hub sample transport, and results return the same way. Some sites run point-of-care VL on GeneXpert. Lower limit of detection varies by platform, so print '<LDL' as the lab sends it. One result, shown as copies/mL plus log10. minLevel is a judgement: the bulk of testing is central at CPHL.

orderLoinc.longName: HLA-B27 [Presence] by NAA with probe detection

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: Section 'molecular' because send-out HLA-B27 is most often by PCR (SSP or real-time). Flow cytometry is a screening alternative (code 26028-1) but needs fresh blood within 24-48 h, which suits referral poorly. Referral test via private labs, usually sent abroad; kit-dependent only for flow cut-offs.

tests.specimen: Self-collected vaginal swab or clinician-collected cervical sample
tests.container: Kit transport vial (e.g. PreservCyt / Xpert HPV collection kit); dry swab where the kit allows
tests.notes: Primary cervical screening for women aged 30–49 (25–49 living with HIV), in line with the national scale-up. Results come Xpert-style: HPV 16, HPV 18/45, other HR, plus an overall high-risk result. HPV-positive → triage/treat (VIA, thermal ablation/cryotherapy) per the national screen-and-treat algorithm. No LOINC order panel matches the Xpert channel grouping. minLevel, route and age bands are judgements to confirm against the current MoH guideline.

orderLoinc.longName: Influenza virus types A and B panel - Upper respiratory specimen by NAA with probe detection

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: Mostly sentinel ILI/SARI surveillance through UVRI (National Influenza Centre), which subtypes influenza A positives. Clinical ordering is mainly at private labs. Component codes are the 'Respiratory system specimen' ones, so they can be shared with the 4-plex panel (see gaps).

tests.specimen: Sputum (smear- or Xpert-positive) or culture isolate
tests.container: Sterile sputum container, 2–8 °C, triple-packaged via hub

orderLoinc.longName: MTB complex rifAMPin and isoniazid resistance panel by Molecular genetics method

tests.notes: Done at NTRL. Detects INH resistance (katG vs inhA pattern) and confirms RIF resistance. Usually ordered with culture and phenotypic DST.

tests.specimen: Sputum or culture isolate from an RR/MDR-TB patient
tests.container: Sterile sputum container, 2–8 °C, triple-packaged via hub

orderLoinc.longName: Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex resistance panel by Molecular genetics method

tests.notes: Done at NTRL for confirmed RR/MDR-TB. Gives fluoroquinolone and second-line injectable resistance. Xpert MTB/XDR is replacing it where available.

tests.specimen: Lesion swab (vesicle fluid/roof, or crust), 2 lesions; oropharyngeal swab if no lesions
tests.container: Dry sterile tube or VTM, 2–8 °C, triple-packaged

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: The reference lab confirms cases and reports clade (Ib in the 2024–2025 Uganda outbreak). Notifiable. Specimens go through the outbreak sample transport, not routine clinical lab benches. The order panel 101398-6 (Mpox + non-variola orthopoxvirus) was not opened, so it is not used.

tests.container: Flocked swab in viral transport medium (VTM), 2–8 °C, triple-packaged

orderLoinc.longName: SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) RNA [Presence] in Respiratory system specimen by NAA with probe detection

tests.notes: Regional PCR capacity and GeneXpert Xpress cartridges were set up during COVID-19, but availability now varies. UVRI/CPHL are the referral labs. Antigen RDT belongs in immunology_serology. minLevel and route are judgements.

tests.display: SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B and RSV PCR

orderLoinc.longName: Influenza virus A and B and SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) and Respiratory syncytial virus RNA panel - Respiratory system specimen by NAA with probe detection

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: One-cartridge GeneXpert multiplex. Mainly at private hospitals and labs. Public sites run it only where cartridges are supplied. minLevel and route are judgements.

tests.specimen: Whole blood (EDTA); oral swab from a deceased suspect
tests.container: EDTA (purple) PLASTIC tube only, no glass; triple packaging (Category A, UN2814)
tests.notes: HIGH-RISK SPECIMEN ROUTE: suspected VHF samples are Category A infectious substances. Trained staff collect in full PPE and notify the district surveillance focal person/DSO. The sample travels by the dedicated VHF courier to the UVRI VHF lab (or an outbreak mobile lab), never by the routine hub or the general lab bench. Do not run routine analysers on the sample before VHF is excluded. Each virus is reported separately. LOINC 88186-2 (Ebola + Marburg panel, verified ACTIVE) covers only two of the six targets, so it was not used as the order code.

tests.specimen: Sputum (or the remaining processed sample from an MTB-positive Xpert run)

orderLoinc.longName: Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex resistance panel by Molecular genetics method

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: Reflex test when MTB is detected and RR-TB is found (fluoroquinolone result guides the BPaLM/BPaL vs longer regimen), or when INH resistance is suspected. Needs 10-colour GeneXpert modules, which only some sites have. minLevel and route are judgements. Kanamycin/capreomycin channels are not stored.

tests.specimen: Pleural, peritoneal (ascitic) or pericardial fluid, or washings; ideally 20–50 mL fresh
tests.container: Sterile universal container, fresh and unfixed; to the lab the same day or 2–8 °C

orderLoinc.longName: Cytology report of Body fluid Cyto stain

tests.notes: Send separate aliquots for chemistry (protein, LDH, glucose, ADA), cell count, Gram stain/culture and Xpert, because those are other tests. Cell block on request. minLevel is a judgement. Makerere University / Mulago Dept of Pathology is the usual public referral route, but it is not in the referTo enum (see gaps). Lancet and other private labs, and UCI for oncology, are the alternatives.

tests.specimen: Trephine core (≥1.5–2 cm) from the posterior iliac crest
tests.container: Formalin pot (10% NBF); the lab decalcifies

orderLoinc.longName: Bone marrow Pathology biopsy report Narrative

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: Bone marrow aspirate smears are a separate haematology test. Send a recent FBC and film report with the request. Used for dry tap, lymphoma staging, aplasia and infiltration; IHC (test.ihc) is often added. minLevel is a judgement. Makerere University / Mulago Dept of Pathology is the usual public referral route, but it is not in the referTo enum (see gaps). Lancet and other private labs, and UCI for oncology, are the alternatives.

tests.specimen: FFPE block from breast core biopsy or excision (fixed 6–72 h in 10% NBF)
tests.container: Paraffin block plus H&E slide in a block box
tests.notes: Guides endocrine therapy and anti-HER2 therapy. HER2 2+ needs reflex ISH, which is often referred abroad. Cold ischaemia should be under 1 hour and fixation 6–72 h, or results are unreliable. No LOINC order panel was opened for this grouping. Offered at UCI, Makerere pathology and private labs. Route is a judgement.

tests.container: Sterile plain tube; to the lab within 1 hour (cells degrade quickly)

orderLoinc.longName: Cytology report of Specimen Cyto stain

tests.notes: For suspected leptomeningeal malignancy (lymphoma, leukaemia, metastatic carcinoma). The order code is the generic 'Specimen' cytology report because no CSF-specific report code was found. Cell count, CrAg and Xpert are separate tests. minLevel is a judgement. Makerere University / Mulago Dept of Pathology is the usual public referral route, but it is not in the referTo enum (see gaps). Lancet and other private labs, and UCI for oncology, are the alternatives.

tests.specimen: Aspirate from a palpable or image-guided lesion (thyroid, breast, lymph node, salivary gland, soft tissue)
tests.container: Labelled glass slides, some air-dried and some alcohol-fixed; needle rinse in saline/RPMI or formalin for a cell block

orderLoinc.longName: Cytology report of Tissue fine needle aspirate Cyto stain

tests.notes: Usually done by the pathologist (FNA clinic) or under ultrasound guidance. The diagnosis line uses the site's reporting system (thyroid Bethesda, breast IAC Yokohama). If TB lymphadenitis is suspected, send a separate rinse for GeneXpert (test.tb_xpert). minLevel is a judgement. Makerere University / Mulago Dept of Pathology is the usual public referral route, but it is not in the referTo enum (see gaps). Lancet and other private labs, and UCI for oncology, are the alternatives.

tests.container: Dry sterile container or saline-moistened gauze, carried to the lab at once

orderLoinc.longName: Pathology report intraoperative observation in Specimen Document

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: Book in advance with the pathologist. It cannot be referred: it needs an on-site cryostat and pathologist while the patient is in theatre, so it is effectively unavailable at a typical RRH. Always send the remaining tissue for paraffin histology (test.histology_biopsy) for the final diagnosis. minLevel is a judgement.

tests.specimen: Tissue: incisional/excisional, core, endoscopic or curettage biopsy, or resection
tests.container: Formalin pot, 10% neutral buffered formalin at ≥10× tissue volume; wide-mouth for large specimens

orderLoinc.longName: Surgical pathology study

tests.notes: Report as text sections: specimen, clinical details, macroscopic, microscopic, diagnosis, comment. A complete request form (site, clinical summary, previous histology numbers) is essential. Turnaround is days to weeks. Run in-house only where an RRH has a pathologist (minLevel is a judgement). Makerere University / Mulago Dept of Pathology is the usual public referral route, but it is not in the referTo enum (see gaps). Lancet and other private labs, and UCI for oncology, are the alternatives.

tests.specimen: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue block from prior histology
tests.container: Paraffin block plus H&E slide in a block box; copy of the original histology report

orderLoinc.longName: Immune stain study

tests.notes: Referral only, usually requested by the pathologist (e.g. lymphoma typing, tumour of unknown origin, Kaposi sarcoma HHV-8). Offered at Makerere pathology, UCI and private labs (Lancet). Some panels go abroad. Antibody list and results are given in the supplementary report. Route is a judgement.

tests.specimen: Cervical sample (Cervex broom/brush) rinsed into the LBC vial

orderLoinc.longName: Cytology report of Cervical or vaginal smear or scraping Cyto stain.thin prep

levelBasis.note: Not on the 2017 national menu; strand judgement

tests.notes: Same Bethesda concepts as the conventional Pap; only the order code differs. The same vial can be used for reflex/co-test HPV DNA. Mainly at private labs (e.g. Lancet) and UCI. Route is a judgement.

tests.specimen: Ectocervical and endocervical scrape (Ayre spatula + cytobrush)
tests.container: Frosted-end glass slide labelled in pencil, fixed immediately (95% ethanol or spray fixative), in a slide box

orderLoinc.longName: Cytology report of Cervical or vaginal smear or scraping Cyto stain

tests.notes: Reported in Bethesda 2014 categories, coded. In the public programme, VIA and HPV testing are the main screening tests; Pap is used where cytology services exist (UCI, Mulago/Makerere, private labs, some RRHs). Not proposed as restricted because it is a cancer screening result; the CSO may decide otherwise. minLevel and route are judgements.

loinc.longName: Erythrocyte [Morphology] in Blood

concepts.notes: Free-text description as Ugandan labs write it (e.g. 'microcytic hypochromic, target cells, occasional sickle cells'). LOINC scale is Nom; MedSync stores text until a coded morphology value set is agreed.

loinc.longName: Leukocytes [Morphology] in Blood

concepts.notes: Free text, e.g. toxic granulation, hypersegmented neutrophils, atypical lymphocytes, blasts seen. LOINC scale is Nom.

loinc.longName: Platelets [Morphology] in Blood

concepts.notes: Free text: adequacy on film, clumps, giant platelets. LOINC scale is Nom.

loinc.longName: Morphology [Interpretation] in Blood Narrative

concepts.notes: The haematologist's or lab scientist's overall impression and suggested further tests, e.g. 'Features suggestive of iron deficiency; suggest ferritin'. This is what clinicians call the 'film comment'.

loinc.longName: Reticulocytes/Erythrocytes in Blood

concepts.notes: Method-neutral code chosen because most Ugandan labs count manually (new methylene blue or brilliant cresyl blue). Automated analysers can map to the 'by Automated count' term instead.

loinc.longName: Reticulocytes [#/volume] in Blood

concepts.notes: Calculated from retic % x RBC count when done manually; analyser-derived on automated platforms.

loinc.longName: Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood by Centrifugation

concepts.notes: Manual spun PCV (microhaematocrit centrifuge). Kept separate from obs.haematocrit (analyser-derived, LOINC 4544-3) because the method differs.

loinc.longName: Hemoglobin S [Presence] in Blood

concepts.notes: Method-neutral HbS presence term so that both the sodium metabisulphite slide test and the dithionite solubility tube test fit. A positive result cannot tell trait (AS) from disease (SS); confirm with HemoTypeSC, electrophoresis or HPLC. A lab that only runs the solubility test can map to 6864-3 'Hemoglobin S [Presence] in Blood by Solubility test' (verified ACTIVE).
No LOINC code for this; it is metadata that tells the reader how far to trust the result.

loinc.longName: Hemoglobin pattern [Interpretation] in Blood

concepts.notes: One concept shared by the point-of-care sickle test (HemoTypeSC-type, which detects A, S and C only, so HbS_beta_thal and other_variant are lab-only answers) and the electrophoresis/HPLC report. Recent transfusion (about 3 months) can give a false pattern; record it on the request.

loinc.longName: Hemoglobin A/Hemoglobin.total in Blood

concepts.notes: Method-neutral term so HPLC and capillary electrophoresis results both fit. HPLC-specific code 42244-4 is a member of panel 94537-8.

loinc.longName: Hemoglobin A2/Hemoglobin.total in Blood

concepts.notes: HbA2 is raised in beta-thalassaemia trait and falsely raised by HbS on some HPLC columns; the method matters.

loinc.longName: Hemoglobin F/Hemoglobin.total in Blood

concepts.notes: Used to monitor hydroxyurea response in sickle cell disease. Physiologically high in infants under 6 months.

loinc.longName: Hemoglobin S/Hemoglobin.total in Blood

concepts.notes: Used to target HbS below 30% after exchange or top-up transfusion (stroke prevention).

loinc.longName: Hemoglobin C/Hemoglobin.total in Blood
Hemoglobins that can be presumptively identified based on available controls in DBS

concepts.notes: Isoelectric focusing pattern from CPHL, listed in order of quantity (F first in infants). The LOINC answer list (LL1511-6) codes each haemoglobin separately; MedSync keeps the combined pattern as one coded answer and can expand it to multiple LOINC answers on export.

loinc.longName: Glucose-6-Phosphate dehydrogenase [Presence] in Red Blood Cells

concepts.notes: Fluorescent spot test or rapid lateral-flow test. Heterozygous females can screen normal; a recent haemolytic episode or transfusion can give a false normal result.

loinc.longName: Glucose-6-Phosphate dehydrogenase [Enzymatic activity/mass] in Red Blood Cells

concepts.notes: Spectrophotometric assay or a quantitative point-of-care biosensor (which also measures Hb). Report against the kit's own normal median.

loinc.longName: Fibrinogen [Mass/volume] in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay

concepts.notes: Clauss functional assay. Key in postpartum haemorrhage and DIC.

loinc.longName: Thrombin time

concepts.notes: Prolonged by heparin, dabigatran, low or abnormal fibrinogen and FDPs.

loinc.longName: Coagulation factor VIII activity actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay

concepts.notes: One-stage clotting assay. 1% is treated as equal to 1 IU/dL. Used to diagnose and grade haemophilia A.

loinc.longName: Coagulation factor IX activity actual/normal in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay

concepts.notes: One-stage clotting assay. Used to diagnose and grade haemophilia B.

loinc.longName: dRVVT actual/normal (normalized LA screen)

concepts.notes: Patient dRVVT divided by normal pooled plasma dRVVT. LOINC's example unit is %, but labs report it as a ratio (e.g. 1.25).

loinc.longName: dRVVT/dRVVT.excess phospholipid [Ratio] normalized in Platelet poor plasma by Coagulation assay
Lupus anticoagulant two screening tests W Reflex [interpretation]

concepts.notes: Generic code 3281-3 'Lupus anticoagulant [Interpretation] in Platelet poor plasma' is DISCOURAGED by LOINC, so the two-screening-test (aPTT-LA + dRVVT) interpretation term is used instead. The answers follow the CLSI answer list LL3015-6.

loinc.longName: Bleeding time

concepts.notes: Duke (earlobe) or Ivy method. Obsolete: poorly reproducible and does not predict surgical bleeding. Kept only because Ugandan request forms still list it.

loinc.longName: Clotting time of Blood by Lee White method

concepts.notes: Obsolete whole-blood clotting time. LOINC's example unit is seconds; Ugandan labs report minutes.
Bedside test for venom-induced coagulopathy after snakebite: 2 mL of venous blood in a new, clean, dry glass tube, left undisturbed for 20 minutes, then tipped once. No LOINC code found.

loinc.longName: Bone marrow aspiration report

concepts.notes: Narrative report: site, cellularity, M:E ratio, differential, iron stain, conclusion. LOINC scale is Doc. A trephine biopsy is reported by histopathology.

loinc.longName: Leukocytes [#/volume] in Cerebrospinal Fluid

concepts.notes: Reported as cells/mm3 (= /uL) from a counting chamber (Neubauer or Fuchs-Rosenthal).

loinc.longName: Neutrophils/Leukocytes in Cerebrospinal Fluid
Lymphocytes/Leukocytes in Cerebrospinal Fluid
Erythrocytes [#/volume] in Cerebrospinal Fluid

concepts.notes: Helps interpret a traumatic tap.

loinc.longName: Leukocytes [#/volume] in Body fluid

concepts.notes: LOINC system 'Body fluid'; the fluid type (pleural, ascitic, synovial, pericardial) is recorded on the specimen. LOINC's example unit is 10*3/uL; Ugandan labs report cells/mm3.

loinc.longName: Neutrophils/Leukocytes in Body fluid
Lymphocytes/Leukocytes in Body fluid
Neutrophils [#/volume] in Body fluid

concepts.notes: WBC x neutrophil %. For ascitic fluid this is the spontaneous bacterial peritonitis threshold value, so it is reported explicitly. The peritoneal-specific term 26502-5 'Neutrophils [#/volume] in Peritoneal fluid' (verified ACTIVE) can be used on export when the specimen is ascitic fluid.

loinc.longName: Erythrocytes [#/volume] in Body fluid
Blood group antibody screen [Presence] in Serum or Plasma

concepts.notes: An IAT against group O screening cells. A positive result needs antibody identification (refer).

loinc.longName: Blood group antibody screen [Titer] in Serum or Plasma

concepts.notes: Usually anti-D in a sensitised RhD-negative pregnancy. When the antibody has been identified as anti-D, 1304-5 'D Ab [Titer] in Serum or Plasma' (verified ACTIVE) is the more specific export code.

loinc.longName: Blood product unit ID [#]

concepts.notes: The UBTS donation/unit number on the bag label. LOINC models it as Qn with unit {ID}; MedSync stores it as text because unit numbers can contain letters.
Crossmatch is for red-cell-containing components. No LOINC code verified.

concepts.display: Donor unit ABO and RhD group

gaps: The Uganda national menu (S1, March 2017) was opened in full. Table 1 is a rotated landscape table where each level column is an independent list (rows are not aligned across columns). Levels were reconstructed from PDF text coordinates by assigning each item to its column band. A few wrapped cell fragments may be merged or split, so spot-check against the PDF pages cited.

S1's narrative (s.2.2.1-2.2.5) and Table 1 disagree in places. PT and CSF analysis: narrative says HC IV, table says GH. Thyroid, fertility hormones and cardiac profile: narrative says GH, table says RRH. HbA1c and Hb electrophoresis: narrative says RRH, table says NRH only. Culture and sensitivity: narrative says RRH, table puts bacterial ID/AST at GH. Plasmin inhibitor: narrative says GH/NRH, table lists all levels. Lipids: narrative says GH, table puts total cholesterol and triglycerides at HC IV. minLevel follows the table; each conflict is noted in its evidence field. A product decision is needed on which to trust; the narrative is arguably the stated policy intent.

Several Table 1 group headings (Reticulocyte test, Body fluid analysis, Mycology, Histology/Cytology, Blood gases, Thyroid, Fertility hormones, Tumour markers, Cardiac profile, Lipid profile, LFTs, RFTs, Electrolytes) span all five columns but have no child tests at the lower levels. They were treated as section headings, not tests.

S1 has no HC II column. Policy says no laboratories below HC III. HC II entries come only from s.2.2.7: six POC tests (HIV, malaria, HBV, syphilis, pregnancy, glucose). Other commonly used POC tests at HC II (e.g. Hb by HemoCue, urine dipstick, MUAC is not a lab test) are not in an opened source.

S10 (UNIPH 2024) states the number of tests on the national menu per level: RRH 146, GH 85, HC IV 57, HC III 31 (2011/2017 test menu as used by NHLDS). The Table 1 reconstruction here has more granular rows grouped into ~150 menu lines, so counts will not match one-to-one. S10 also reports that 68 of 146 tests have no DHIS2 data-entry field. This matters for MedSync-DHIS2 mapping.

Not opened (web search budget exhausted, or the source was not reachable): MoH Health Sector Service Standards 2016, the EMHSLU laboratory section, any revised (post-2017) national test menu, UBTS and UCI own websites, and Makerere/Mulago pathology department pages. No newer edition of the NSTMT was found on the CPHL library page (listed as 'NSTMT TEST MENU.pdf', the 2017 document).

UVRI VHF: the VHF case investigation form routes samples to the UVRI/CDC VHF lab but does not name pathogens. Ebola/Marburg naming is a judgement. Arbovirus and measles/polio roles come from UVRI web pages, which do not describe the sample-routing mechanism.
UCI entries come from S1 Table 2, whose column bands overlapped (tumour markers / IHC / serology). Attribution to UCI is reliable, but sub-column placement is approximate.

WHO EDL: eEDL shows the 'Fifth WHO Model List' but no publication date. The WHO IVD selection page still showed EDL4 (Oct 2023). Setting assignment per test was read from eEDL entries; 'NL' means the test appears in both settings, often with different assay formats (e.g. glucose POC vs analyser).
S1 Table 1 also appears to include some header noise (e.g. stray page numbers). These were excluded.
